svg.title: Chronic pain: pain over 3 months is mostly a processing problem, so everyone gets education and supervised exercise first; then the drug is matched to what the pain looks like (tissue source, neuropathic, poor sleep, low mood), adjuvants come before opioids, and a patient who is not responding is referred and gets an opioid trial only under the START principle; below, acute vs subacute vs chronic pain, what each team member does, and which opioid to step to and how to switch

svg.text: mostly a PROCESSING problem (sensitized nervous system) · goal = manage pain and function, NOT cure

svg.text: acute phase first: fully investigate and treat the injury, then early return to low-impact activity

svg.text: • EDUCATE: hurt does NOT equal harm; the injury has healed, so activity desensitizes

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • EXERCISE, individualized and SUPERVISED: strength + flexibility + cardio (yoga, tai chi for back pain); good evidence

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • passive modalities (transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), ultrasound, laser, heat): very little evidence

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • massage only WITH exercise and education
